info.name: Kabil.ai Backend
info.description:
Manual-test collection for the Kabil.ai FastAPI backend.

Covers every endpoint shipped through Step 2.5:

- Health
- Auth (Login / Me / Logout)
- Jobs (Create / List / Get / Patch Status / Get & Patch WhatsApp Questions)

## Setup

1. Import this file plus `kabil-backend.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **Kabil.ai — Local Dev** environment in the top-right dropdown.
3. Fill in `admin_email` + `admin_password` with the credentials produced by `make seed`.
4. Run **Login (Success)** — the response's `access_token` is auto-saved to `{{access_token}}` and used by every authenticated request.
5. Run **Me** to verify the token works.
6. Under **Jobs**, run **Create Job** — `{{job_id}}` is captured and used by the subsequent Job requests.

## Server

The API must be running locally (default port 8000). Start it with `make up` (Docker) or `make dev` (hot reload outside Docker).

request.description:
Paginated list. Enable the `status` and `search` query params to filter (case-insensitive substring match on `title`). Max `page_size` is 100; items ordered by `updated_at DESC`.

Each item carries `applications_by_stage` — the per-job pipeline funnel counting that job's applications at each stage (`vector_screen` … `done`). Always fully populated (every stage key present, zero-filled); counts all applications regardless of status.

Full detail (omits `jd_embedding` and `ai_verify_flags`). Response is cached in Redis for 60 s using a key versioned by `updated_at` — any write rotates the key naturally, so no explicit invalidation runs.

Move job from draft → open. Step 2.6 will enqueue JD embedding + WhatsApp question generation on this transition; today the endpoint just flips status. Only `open` and `closed` are accepted as the target status.
Move job from open → closed. Sets `closed_at` server-side. Run *after* Open.
After running the Open + Close patches above, the job is in `closed`. Attempting `closed → closed` (or any non-allowed edge) returns 409. The allowed matrix is draft→open, open→closed, closed→open.

Each item carries `ai_verifies_response` (default `false`); only questions with `ai_verifies_response=true` (the AI `background_validation` questions) have the candidate's reply AI-scored. item.name: Public
item.description:
Public-facing endpoints that candidates hit without authentication.

These routes are reached via per-job shareable slugs minted by HR (`PublicUploadToken.slug`); the slug acts as the only access control. Honeypot, slug-active, consent, and PDF-validation checks are enforced server-side.

formdata.description: Bot-trap field. Leave empty in the real client. Any non-empty value short-circuits to a fake 202 with no DB writes.
Pick any PDF. Magic-byte and size validation are server-side; max size lives in settings.cv_max_file_size_mb.

request.description:
Submit a CV against a public job slug. Returns 202 with `{reference_number: <UUID hex>}` and enqueues the Step 3.9 CV processing chain (extract → parse → authenticity → embed → similarity → auto_reject).

**Idempotency:**
- Same candidate (email + phone) applying twice to the same job returns the *same* reference number (unique on `(candidate_id, job_id)`).
- Same PDF bytes re-uploaded for the same candidate reuse the existing `cv_documents` row (sha256-keyed dedup).
- New PDF bytes for an existing candidate insert a fresh `cv_documents` row and rotate the `is_current` flag.

**Test script** captures `reference_number` into `{{application_reference_number}}`.

item.name: Applications
item.description:
Step 4.1 HR endpoints over the `applications` table.

- `GET /jobs/{job_id}/applications` — paginated list with stage/status filters and ordering. Cached in Redis for 15 s per (job_id, filter set, page).
- `GET /applications/{id}` — full detail with nested candidate, current CV, and chronological score history.
- `GET /applications/{id}/audit-log` — newest-first audit entries (Step 4.2 wires the first writes).

All endpoints require HR auth (`Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`).

request.description:
Paginated list of applications submitted to the given job. Cached for 15 s per (job_id, stage, status, order, page, page_size). 404 if the job id is unknown.

**Test script** captures the first item's id into `{{application_id}}` so the Detail / Audit-Log requests can run without manual copy/paste.
Exercises the `status` filter. Useful after Step 3.9 auto-rejection has flipped low-similarity rows to `rejected` (stage stays `vector_screen` so HR can see why they were dropped).

request.description: Best matches first; NULLs (rows not yet through Step 3.9's similarity step) land last so the top of the page is always meaningful.

Full nested detail: application row + candidate snapshot + current CV reference + chronological `application_scores` history (newest first). 404 if the application id is unknown.

`whatsapp_sessions` and `interview_slots` will be added when Phase 5 / 6 introduces those tables.
Chronological (newest first) audit log for one application. Empty until Step 4.2 starts writing on stage/status transitions. 404 if the application id is unknown.

exec: // Inbound free-text answers carry per-answer scores (0-10).
const scored = data.messages.filter(m => m.answer_relevance_score !== null && m.answer_relevance_score !== undefined);
pm.test("scored answers expose relevance + ai fields", () => {

request.description:
HR-facing screening transcript for one application: the conversation state-machine cursor (`state`, `current_question_index`), the structured `answers[]` copy, and the full ordered `messages[]` transcript HR renders as the chat.

Each inbound free-text answer message carries per-answer scoring (Claude Haiku, Step 5.4) so HR can triage replies at a glance:
- `answer_relevance_score` (0-10) — how directly the answer addresses the question (10 = fully on-topic).
- `answer_ai_score` (0-10) — how AI-generated the answer reads (10 = almost certainly AI-written; **higher is the worse signal**).
- `answer_score_rationale` — one short HR-facing note explaining both scores.

These three fields are `null` on every non-answer row (greeting, questions, button taps, closing) and `null` on an answer if scoring failed (best-effort — a scoring miss never blocks screening). The same scores also appear inside each `answers[]` entry (`relevance_score` / `ai_likelihood_score` / `rationale`).

Returns 404 (`error=whatsapp_conversation_not_found`) until HR moves the application into the `whatsapp` stage and the invite runs.
Asserts the global exception handler maps `ApplicationNotFoundError` → HTTP 404 with `error=application_not_found`.

Move the application through the pipeline. Allowed transitions:
- `vector_screen → hard_filter`
- `hard_filter → whatsapp`
- `whatsapp → interview`
- `interview → done`

Moving to `hard_filter` enqueues the Step 4.3 scoring task (currently stubbed: marks `pipeline_status.hard_filter = 'pending'`). The audit log records before / after state with HR identity and the optional `reason`. The list cache for the parent job is invalidated.

Stage moves require `status=active`; rejected/accepted applications return 422.

Invalid transitions return 422 with `error=illegal_stage_transition`.
Skipping `hard_filter` directly to `whatsapp` is not in the allow-list and returns 422.

Flip the application's `status`. Allowed:
- `active → rejected`
- `active → accepted`
- `rejected → active` (HR override, stage preserved)

`accepted` is terminal — further status changes return 422.

The audit log records `manually_rejected` / `manually_accepted` / `status_changed` (override path) with the optional `reason`. Stage is intentionally not modified.
HR override: bring a rejected candidate back into the pipeline at the stage they were rejected from.
Once an application is `accepted` it is terminal; any further status change returns 422. Run `Patch Status (Reject)` first if the captured application is still active.

HR-triggered manual rescore. Writes a `rescore_requested` audit-log row, then dispatches the Step 4.3 scoring task with `force=True`:

- skips the idempotent-skip on the existing `hard_filter_score`,
- nulls the existing score + breakdown so the detail endpoint shows 'in progress' until the new run lands,
- bypasses the Claude Redis cache (`use_cache=False`) so HR genuinely gets a fresh Sonnet response, not a cached one.

The `application_scores` audit table retains the prior attempt; a new row is appended for the rescore. Returns 202 immediately; the new value becomes visible on the detail endpoint after the worker finishes.

Re-runs cosine similarity scoring. Since the underlying CV/JD embeddings are deterministic, the cache bypass is a no-op for similarity -- `force=True` here just means 'recompute against the latest embeddings'. Useful after a CV re-upload or a JD edit (the latter would also re-embed the JD).
Pydantic enum validation rejects unknown rescore types before the route body runs.

item.name: Bulk Upload CVs (HR — up to 50 PDFs)

formdata.description: Pick one PDF. The endpoint accepts up to 50 — duplicate this row in Postman (use the ⋮ menu → 'Add row' and key it 'files') to attach more in one request. Each file is independently validated; bad ones come back in `rejected` with a reason.
Second file slot — leave blank if you only want to test one.
Third file slot — leave blank if you only want to test one or two.

request.description:
HR-only endpoint for uploading a batch of CVs against one job. Up to 50 PDFs per request, 10 MB each.

**Per-file processing (synchronous inside the request):**
1. PDF magic-byte + size check.
2. Batch-level sha256 dedup (second occurrence rejected as `duplicate_in_batch`).
3. Upload to Azure Blob (idempotent by sha256).
4. pypdf text extraction (Redis-cached).
5. Claude Haiku contact extraction (Redis-cached) for name + email + phone.
6. Phone normalised to E.164.
7. Find-or-create candidate on `(LOWER(email), phone_e164)`.
8. If the candidate already applied to this job → response lands the file in `already_applied`, no new application created.
9. Otherwise create the `cv_document` + `application` and enqueue the Step 3.9 CV pipeline.

**Rejection reasons:**
- `not_pdf` — magic-byte mismatch
- `too_large` — exceeds `cv_max_file_size_mb`
- `duplicate_in_batch` — same sha256 as an earlier file in *this* request
- `parse_failed_no_contact` — Claude couldn't surface enough to create a Candidate (name OR email OR phone missing/unnormalisable)

**Concurrency:** blob upload + text extraction + Claude calls fan out under `asyncio.Semaphore(10)`.

**Audit log:** one row per newly-created application plus one batch-summary row keyed on the job; both share `after_state.batch_id`.

**Test script** captures `batch_id` and the first created application's id/candidate_id into the environment for follow-up requests.

request.description: Bulk upload is refused unless the target job is `status='open'`. Draft and closed jobs both yield 422 with `error=job_not_open_for_applications`. Point `{{closed_job_id}}` at a job whose status is `closed` or `draft` to exercise this branch — the easiest setup is to run the **Patch Status (Close)** request first and reuse its `{{job_id}}`.

item.name: Talent Pool
item.description:
Phase 7 talent-pool surface. HR keeps strong candidates in a pool and later sources them onto jobs.

- **Add to Pool** — pool an existing candidate (needs `{{candidate_id}}`).
- **Upload CV to Pool** — drop a PDF straight into the pool; identity is parsed from the CV, candidate created, and the parse/authenticity/embed pipeline runs so they're searchable. Sets `{{candidate_id}}` + `{{talent_pool_entry_id}}`.
- **Search Pool** — semantic search over pooled candidates' CVs (ranked by cosine similarity, highest first). Needs an embedded CV — run Upload first and give the worker a moment.
- **List Pool** — paginated listing.
- **Source to Job** — create a fresh application (L1, full scoring) for a pooled candidate against `{{job_id}}`; sets `{{application_id}}`.
- **Candidate History** — the candidate's full cross-job journey: one scored stint per application they ever had (live or archived), each with its scores + WhatsApp screening digest. Needs `{{candidate_id}}`.

request.description: Add an existing candidate to the pool (idempotent on the candidate). `source_job_id` is optional — where they came from. Returns 201 with the entry + candidate snapshot.

formdata.description: Pick one CV PDF. Identity (name/email/phone) is parsed from the file; a CV with no usable contact is rejected 422. After the response, the worker parses + embeds the CV so it shows up in Search Pool.

request.description: Upload a CV directly into the talent pool — no job, no application. Returns 201 with the pool entry, candidate, and `enqueued` (whether the embed pipeline was dispatched).

Semantic search over the pool. `q` is embedded and pooled candidates are ranked by cosine similarity of their current CV (0-100 `similarity_score`, highest first). Candidates without an embedded CV are excluded.
List pool entries, newest first, with candidate snapshots.

Source a pooled candidate onto `{{job_id}}`. Creates a fresh application at vector_screen flagged `sourced_from_talent_pool` and runs the full CV scoring pipeline. Idempotent on (candidate, job) → `already_existed=true`.

The candidate's entire cross-job journey: one stint per application they ever had — live, rejected, accepted, or archived (moved back to the pool) — each with the scores + WhatsApp screening digest computed against that job. Candidate-level authenticity is surfaced once on the `candidate` snapshot. This is what powers "see the candidate's full history, scored against every job they were part of" from the pool. `404` if the candidate is unknown.
